subject: Hospitality
title: Regenerative Tourism
description: A micro-lesson that makes Regenerative Tourism usable.

hook.text: Sustainability means doing less harm. Regenerative tourism goes further—leaving a place better than you found it.

buildup.text: Regenerative hotels invest in local ecosystems, hire from nearby communities, and restore cultural heritage.

discovery.text: New Zealand and Costa Rica lead in regenerative tourism—travelers plant trees, restore reefs, and fund schools.

twist.text: Critics warn that 'regenerative' could become the next greenwashing buzzword if hotels don't prove measurable impact.

climax.text: The best regenerative programs track outcomes: coral regrowth, species counts, and community income over years.

punchline.text: Don't just visit. Leave it better. That's the regenerative promise.

quiz.question: How does regenerative tourism differ from sustainable tourism?
options: It aims to leave places better, not just less harmed
